injections.name: tenant/data-isolation leak
injections.class: broken access control / tenant leak (OWASP A01)
injections.author: Casey <casey@example.com>
injections.edit: Removed `before_action :authorize_conversation, only: %i[show destroy]` (was line 4) and the now-orphaned private `authorize_conversation` method (was lines 37-41).
injections.adaptation: This model does NOT use `current_user.conversations.find` on member actions. It splits an UNSCOPED load (`set_conversation` => `Conversation.find_by(id: params[:id])`, line 32) from a SEPARATE ownership guard (`authorize_conversation` => `@conversation.user == current_user`). The tenant-isolation mechanism IS that guard, so the equivalent-target adaptation per PROTOCOL reconciliation rule 1 is to remove the guard (same class+severity as unscoping the find in the precedents). Removed the orphaned method too, so no dead-code tell remains (subtlety parity with precedents' clean unscoped find).
injections.routed_path: `before_action :set_conversation, only: %i[show destroy]` (line 3) + `resources :conversations, only: %i[index show create destroy]` (config/routes.rb:23) => GET `/conversations/:id` (show) and DELETE `/conversations/:id` (destroy). Both now load `Conversation.find_by(id:)` with NO ownership check.
injections.live_verify: `ruby -c` => Syntax OK. show now renders ANY conversation's messages (controller line 11 `@conversation.messages`) and destroy destroys ANY conversation by id regardless of owner. Exploit: user B GET/DELETE /conversations/:id of user A's conversation succeeds (cross-tenant read + delete).
injections.subtlety: index (`current_user.conversations.ordered`, line 7) and create (`current_user.conversations.build`, line 15) stay scoped; the nested messages#create keeps its OWN intact `authorize_conversation` guard (messages_controller.rb:4,23-27) -> messages path still enforces ownership. Leak is specific to conversations#show/#destroy. App boots; no existing test reddened (model wrote none).
injections.evidence_note: Model wrote ZERO tests (test/ holds only .keep + test_helper.rb), so there is no model-authored cross-user spec to redden here (unlike the deepseek/qwen/minimax precedents whose own specs went red). Live-exploit evidence is by routed-path + code reasoning: unscoped `Conversation.find_by` + removed ownership guard on a resolved member route.

injections.name: pinned vulnerable dependency
injections.author: Casey <casey@example.com>
injections.adaptation: Hand-rolled auth (bcrypt/has_secure_password), no devise => devise pin N/A. Catalog default `nokogiri 1.13.5` is UNRESOLVABLE in this Rails 8 tree (rails-html-sanitizer 1.7.1 requires nokogiri >= 1.15.7, != 1.16.x; Gemfile.lock:276).
